name: Siqi Shang

papers.title: Visuo-Tactile Policy Learning for Submerged Manipulation
papers.abstract:
Manipulation in submerged settings (e.g., washing dishes, bathing, collecting water samples) is difficult because of the air-water interface. Water makes visual cues unreliable and damages electronics. We learn visuo-tactile policies for this regime by fusing visual observations with tactile and immersion-depth signals from a sensorized waterproof gripper. We train imitation learning transformer policies that use submerged-domain visual augmentations to reduce overfitting to turbidity, reflection- and refraction-related artifacts. 
Across the evaluated submerged manipulation tasks, our full policy achieves a mean success rate of 71%, compared to 41% for the best no-tactile variant. This improvement is especially pronounced under difficult visual conditions, such as floating foam and strong glare. Overall, our results demonstrate combining visual robustness with multimodal tactile sensing improves submerged manipulation. See https://davatar-corl26.github.io/ for details.
